candidate.answerReason: For uniform random sampling without replacement, all three items must come from the six nondefective items. The probability is C(6,3)/C(10,3)=20/120=1/6.

methods.label: Count samples from the nondefective items
methods.levelReason: Counting three-item subsets is a standard elective mathematics method for this sampling problem.

methods.label: Multiply successive nondefective-draw probabilities
methods.explanation:
There are \(10-4=6\) nondefective items. For uniform random sampling without replacement, none of the three drawn items is defective exactly when all three successive draws are nondefective. After each such draw, both the nondefective count and the total count decrease by one. Therefore
\[
P(\text{none defective})
=\frac6{10}\cdot\frac59\cdot\frac48
=\frac16.
\]
methods.levelReason: The probability multiplication rule with changing conditional probabilities is within the same elective mathematics scope and avoids combinations.
